important_evidence: APEX is a deep learning model for antibiotic discovery from extinct organisms, predicts species-specific antibacterial activity against 34 pathogens (from review PMID: 40459283).
AntiBP3 provides a method for predicting ABPs against Gram-positive, Gram-negative, and Gram-variable bacteria, with AUC up to 0.98 on independent test sets.
AMPActiPred is a three-stage deep forest framework for ABP identification and activity prediction, achieving accuracy 87.6% and GMean 82.8%.
Multifunctional AMP Design Framework integrates FBGAN with MIC regression and multifunctional attribute prediction.
HydrAMP is a conditional VAE for generating novel AMPs with tunable creativity.
Several other models (AMPlify, AMPpredMFA, sAMP-pred-GAT, etc.) are mentioned in reviews but lack original publication details.
uncertainties: APEX model details (architecture, code, dataset) need full-text verification of the original paper (Wan, Torres, et al. 2024).
Are the training datasets of AntiBP3 and AMPActiPred publicly available? Current evidence does not provide download links.
Does AMPActiPred have a code repository beyond the web server?
Code availability for the FBGAN-enhanced AMP design framework not reported; full text needed to verify.
Details of models mentioned in the review (e.g., AMPlify, AMPpredMFA) require full-text review of original papers for accurate benchmarking.

The review mentions many other models (e.g., Martínez-Mauricio et al. 2024, Li et al. 2022, Shao et al. 2024) without explicit model names; these may be relevant for future inclusion after full-text review.
